title: token scopes list the webhook events they release
detail: `PatScopeDef.events` takes exact event names (no globs). Holding the scope at read or write level is enough to subscribe, `expandScopeEvents(config, granted)` returns the union. Boot fails when a scope lists an event without a public contract, for example an internal `r.defineEvent`. Revoking a token now has a title and a field label in every bundle locale.

title: patScopeOptionKey for translating token scope labels
detail: The scope labels personal-access-tokens generates from `scopes[domain].label` are English only. `patScopeOptionKey(domain, "read" | "write")` returns their translation key, so an app feature can add the other locales with `r.translations`.
migration: Apps that mount personal-access-tokens and set `requiredLocales` with a locale other than `en` translate each generated scope label (`read`, plus `write` where the domain offers it) under `patScopeOptionKey`.

title: Tenants whose tier excludes API tokens now reach the lockedFallbackScreen
detail: GET /api/schema removed every screen of a feature the tenant has switched off, and the role projection then dropped the navs of other features that pointed at them. The token list screen was gone, so the upgrade screen set via lockedFallbackScreen was never shown. Screens that declare a fallback (and the same-feature screens those fallbacks name) now stay in the schema; the server still rejects their queries and writes with feature_disabled, which makes the renderer show the fallback. Navs, content collections and workspaces of the disabled feature are still removed.

title: The token list looks like any other Kumiko list
detail: The create button now sits in the page header next to the title, and an empty list shows the standard hint with a create button. The German title of the list screen is "API-Tokens" instead of "Personal Access Tokens", which also fixes the breadcrumb of the mint screen. Renderer, all apps: a projection list without an entity create button now shows its first primary toolbar action (one that needs no confirmation dialog) in the page header on desktop as well, with its label, instead of in the toolbar row; on phones it already did. On desktop only an icon derived from the action id (or declared on the action) is shown; the plus fallback exists only on phones. Consumers get this after the bump without code changes.

title: The token list screen takes a description and slots via listScreen
detail: createPersonalAccessTokensFeature({ listScreen: { description, slots } }) sets the i18n description and the slots (for example a header component) of the api-tokens list, so an app can show instructions above the list and use the bundled screen directly instead of embedding it in its own dashboard. Without the option nothing changes. Both bundled token screens are now marked agent: { expose: false }, since the mint screen reveals the token plaintext.

title: revokeAllPatTokensForUser detects begin() the same way as the transaction helpers
detail: The transaction probe looked for begin() directly on the handle, so a pool wrapped by a legacy Drizzle connection fell back to a non-atomic update plus append. It now uses runnerCanBeginTransaction from bun-db, which unwraps the client first.

title: API-token screens hide behind the tier gate and can fall back to an upgrade screen via lockedFallbackScreen
detail:
Token screens follow the tier gate of personal-access-tokens
The list and mint screens carry a `visibleWhen` on the new `personal-access-tokens:query:availability` probe. For a tenant whose tier excludes the feature (`toggleable`), the dispatcher already rejected every token handler with `feature_disabled`; now the screens also show the unavailable notice instead of an empty list with a broken Create button. A new option `lockedFallbackScreen` names a screen (for example an upgrade notice) to show in its place. Without `toggleable` nothing changes: the feature stays always on.

title: PAT revoke and its revoked-event commit atomically when called on a pool
The token list status column shows translated labels instead of raw status values
personal-access-tokens: `write:create` now requires `currentPassword` (+ `mfaCode` if MFA enrolled) (e91d4cb).
detail: `personal-access-tokens:write:create` now requires `currentPassword` (verified against the caller's password hash) before minting a token, and rejects when the caller has MFA enrolled and `mfaCode` is missing or wrong — a session cookie alone is no longer enough to stand up a durable API credential. `expiresInDays` now defaults to 90 days instead of never-expiring when omitted (the existing 3650-day cap is unchanged, so a genuinely long-lived token is still possible if requested explicitly). Changing a user's password, or enabling/disabling MFA, now revokes all of that user's live PAT tokens — mirrors the existing session auto-revoke-on-password-change behavior. `run-prod-app`/`run-dev-app` wire the new MFA↔PAT revoke callback automatically when both `auth-mfa` and `personal-access-tokens` are mounted; no app-level change needed for that part.
migration: Apps that already mint PATs (their own client code, scripts, or tests) need to add `currentPassword` to the `create` request payload — this is a breaking change to the `create` request shape despite the minor bump (bundled-features doesn't follow strict semver across its handler schemas yet). If the caller has MFA enrolled, also include a valid `mfaCode`.

title: personal-access-tokens: add `toggleable` option so the whole feature can be tier-gated vi…
detail: personal-access-tokens: add `toggleable` option so the whole feature can be tier-gated via the tier-engine (mirrors ledger/tags). Pass `{ toggleable: { default: false } }` for fail-closed gating — PAT is then off until a tier lists `"personal-access-tokens"` in its features. Omitting the option keeps PAT always-on (no behaviour change for existing consumers).
